lessons.title: Investments vs Expenses: Everything That Counts Under 80C

children.text: Most people think of 80C as a shopping list of tax saving products. Half the list is not products at all. Your daughter's school fees and the principal part of your home loan EMI qualify too, and they often fill the bucket before you invest anything. Knowing the full list, and its fine print, stops you from buying what you do not need and from claiming what you are not allowed to.
Two Buckets That Share One Limit

body.title: What Schedule XV covers under Section 123 (80C)

columns.label: Investments and savings
points: Employee contribution to EPF, plus any VPF
5-year tax saver FD with a scheduled bank, or Post Office 5-year Time Deposit
Your own NPS contribution and insurer pension plans

columns.label: Expenses and payments
points: Life insurance premiums, including term plans
Tuition fees for up to two children
Principal repayment of a home loan
Stamp duty and registration charges on buying a house, in the year paid

body.text: Before you buy a single tax saving product, add up the expenses you are already paying. For many families, they fill most of the ₹1.5 lakh on their own.

children.text: The Master List: Whose Name, How Long Locked

Each item has its own rule on whose name it can be in. Paying your spouse's LIC premium counts. Paying your parents' premium does not. Chapters 2 and 3 cover each product in depth; this table is your reference map.

body.caption: Section 123 (80C) eligible items for an individual taxpayer

3 years per SIP instalment or lump sum
Tax saver FD / Post Office 5-year TD

body.title: Whose Name Counts?
body.question: Rahul, a software architect in Bengaluru on the old regime, pays four premiums this year. Which one can he claim under Section 123 (80C)?
options: Health insurance premium for his parents
LIC policy premium for his retired father
Term insurance premium on his wife's life
Motor insurance premium for his car
body.explanation: Life insurance on self, spouse or children qualifies, so the term plan on his wife counts. Health insurance for parents is a separate deduction (80D, covered in Chapter 4), a life policy on a parent is not eligible for an individual, and motor insurance never qualifies.

children.text: Tuition Fees: Read the Fee Receipt Carefully

Only the tuition fee component counts, for full-time education of up to two children, paid to a school, college, university or other educational institution in India. Development fees, donations, transport, hostel, uniforms and private coaching are all excluded. Your own or your spouse's course fees do not qualify either.

body.title: Your Turn: Find the Eligible Fees
body.prompt: Neha in Delhi pays the following for her two children this year. Child 1: tuition ₹55,000, development fee ₹12,000, school bus ₹18,000. Child 2: tuition ₹48,000, annual activity fee ₹6,000. How much can she claim as tuition fees under Section 123 (80C)?
body.explanation: Only the tuition components count: ₹55,000 + ₹48,000 = ₹1,03,000. The development fee, bus charges and activity fee (₹36,000 in total) are excluded. Ask the school for a fee certificate that shows tuition fees separately, since that is what your employer and the tax department will look for.

body.title: Quick Check
body.textWithBlank: Tuition fees can be claimed under Section 123 (80C) for a maximum of ___ children.
body.explanation: The cap is two children per individual. If both parents are taxpayers, each can claim fees they actually paid, which lets a family with three children cover all three: for example, one parent pays for two and the other pays for the third.

children.text: Home Loans: Principal In, Interest Out

Every home loan EMI has two parts. Only the principal part belongs to 80C. The interest part has its own separate deduction and is not counted here. In the early years of a loan, most of the EMI is interest, so the 80C benefit is smaller than people expect.

body.caption: Aditya, an engineer in Hyderabad: year 3 of a ₹50 lakh home loan from SBI (illustrative split)

cells: Separate home loan interest deduction, not 80C

body.text: Your lender issues a home loan interest certificate every year that shows the exact principal and interest split. Download it from the SBI, HDFC Bank or ICICI Bank app rather than estimating. The loan must be from a specified lender such as a bank, housing finance company or your employer. A loan from a friend or relative does not qualify for the principal deduction.

Not eligible. Tuition fees count only for your children.

cards.definition: Not eligible. Private coaching is not full-time education at an institution.
Not 80C. Interest has a separate deduction with its own limit.

body.text: Some 80C claims can be reversed later. If you sell the house within 5 years from the end of the tax year you got possession, all principal deductions claimed so far are added back to your income in the year of sale. The same clawback applies if you stop a traditional life policy within 2 years or a ULIP within 5 years. Treat these as commitments, not quick tax fixes.

stats.label: Home loan clawback window
stats.context: From the end of the tax year of possession

body.title: Scenario: Sorting the Shoebox
body.scenario: Ravi, a chartered accountant in Ahmedabad on the old regime, brings you his receipts for the tax year: home loan principal ₹90,000 (flat possession received in June 2024), LIC premium on his own life ₹25,000, PPF deposit in his wife's account ₹50,000, tuition fees for two sons ₹60,000, EPF deducted from salary ₹40,000, health insurance for his parents ₹30,000 and a 3-year bank FD of ₹50,000. He also mentions he plans to sell the flat in 2027 and upgrade.
body.prompt: What is Ravi's eligible total, what can he actually claim, which items do not count, and what risk should you flag?
body.modelAnswer: Eligible items: home loan principal ₹90,000, his own LIC ₹25,000, his wife's PPF ₹50,000, tuition fees ₹60,000 and EPF ₹40,000, a total of ₹2,65,000. He can claim only ₹1,50,000. Not eligible: parents' health insurance (a separate 80D deduction) and the 3-year FD (only 5-year tax saver FDs qualify). The risk: possession came in June 2024, which falls in the tax year ending 31 March 2025. If he sells before 31 March 2030, every rupee of home loan principal he has claimed under 80C will be added back to his income in the year of sale. Since his EPF, LIC, PPF and tuition fees alone total ₹1,75,000, he does not even need the home loan principal to fill his limit, so the practical exposure is limited to whatever principal he has actually claimed in past returns. He should check those returns before deciding on the 2027 sale.

body.title: Go Deeper: HUFs and the Fine Print

children.text: For an HUF, life insurance premiums on any member of the HUF qualify, and ELSS can be bought in the HUF's own name. New PPF accounts for HUFs have not been allowed since 2005.
For life insurance, the deduction is capped at 10% of the sum assured for policies issued on or after 1 April 2012 (20% for older policies). Premium above that is not deductible.
Home loan principal repaid before construction is complete and possession is received is generally not eligible. The deduction starts once the house is ready.
Deductions are claimed in the tax year you actually pay. Paying next year's school fees in advance in March counts in the year of payment, not the year the fees relate to.

body.title: Build Your 80C Inventory
steps: Note your employee EPF and VPF from your latest payslip
List every life insurance and ULIP policy on yourself, your spouse and your children, with annual premium
Collect tuition fee certificates for up to two children, tuition component only
Download your home loan certificate and note the principal repaid in the tax year
Add any PPF, SSY, NSC, tax saver FD, SCSS or NPS contributions already made
Remove anything not eligible: health insurance, short FDs, regular mutual funds, parents' policies
Compare your total with ₹1,50,000 to see whether you have a gap at all

points: Section 123 (80C) covers both investments (EPF, PPF, ELSS, NSC, tax saver FD, SCSS, SSY) and expenses (insurance, tuition fees, home loan principal, stamp duty).
Everything shares the same ₹1,50,000 limit, so count existing expenses first.
Each item has a name rule: self, spouse and children for most; parents do not qualify.
Only the tuition component of school fees counts, for up to two children.
Only home loan principal counts. Interest has a separate deduction.
Selling the house within 5 years, or exiting a policy early, can reverse deductions already claimed.
